title: Can Attend All Meetings
statement: You are given a list meetings where each element is a pair [start, end] describing a meeting on a single shared calendar. The pairs arrive in arbitrary order. Treat each meeting as half-open: a meeting occupies the time from start up to but not including end, so a meeting that ends exactly when another begins does NOT conflict (for example [1, 3] and [3, 5] are fine). Return True if one person can attend every meeting without any two overlapping in time, and False otherwise. An empty list and a single meeting both return True.
hints: The meetings come in any order, so before you can reason about which meeting comes right after another, what should you do to the list?
Sort the meetings by their start time; then a conflict can only ever be between a meeting and the one immediately before it in sorted order.

After sorting by start, walk adjacent pairs and return False the moment a meeting's start is strictly less than the previous meeting's end (use < not <=, so back-to-back meetings that merely touch are allowed); if you get through all pairs, return True.
